first.rationale: Current situation shows simultaneous decline in onboarding completion (-4%) and activation (-6%), with competitive pressure on price-sensitive SMBs. Memory 86 (shortening onboarding) and memory 91 (activation messaging) are the most directly relevant to the observed activation deficit. Rather than respond to competitive pricing (which memory 73 warns damages retention), activation_messaging aligns with the product-engagement root cause. Memory 31 supports that signup improvements drive early activation. Activation_messaging is lower-risk than promotional_pricing (which materially harmed retention), and more immediately addressable than enterprise_sales_assist (which targets a different segment). Verification of memories 86 and 91 will confirm whether the activation messaging lever is still viable and whether onboarding improvements should be combined with in-product nudges. This preserves the option to pivot to referral_incentive or enterprise_sales_assist next week if activation_messaging underperforms.

final.rationale: Verification confirms both levers are reliable. Memory_86 shows onboarding shortening drives +13% completion with +3% retention lift. Memory_91 shows activation messaging delivers +6% activation with +1% retention lift—both sustainably improve qualified revenue without the retention damage of promotional_pricing (memory_73). Current -6% activation and -4% onboarding completion declines suggest product-engagement degradation, not pricing sensitivity alone. Activation_messaging is the immediate lever: it directly addresses week-one engagement (-11% impact potential) and compounds with the onboarding improvements already in place. This avoids the retention cliff of promotional_pricing while defending against competitive SMB churn through product stickiness. Enterprise_sales_assist (memory_44) is orthogonal to the self-serve activation problem. Referral_incentive (memory_57) requires healthy activation first to generate qualified referrals. Standard_experiment scale allows measurement without overcommitting; results will inform next week's decision on whether to layer onboarding simplification or test enterprise segment separately.
